SELECT DISTINCT fish_date_doy, fish_date_season 
FROM trips 
WHERE fish_date_season = 6 
ORDER BY fish_date_doy 
LIMIT 5

SELECT ts_doy, ts_hour, ROUND(wtmp_c, 2) as water_temp_c
FROM pier
WHERE ts_season = 6
ORDER BY ts_t DESC
LIMIT 5

SELECT index_id, value, avail_doy 
FROM climate 
WHERE avail_season = 6
ORDER BY avail_doy DESC
LIMIT 5

SELECT cls, COUNT(*) as trips_count, SUM(yt) as total_yt, ROUND(AVG(yt::FLOAT / anglers), 3) as avg_yt_per_angler
FROM trips
WHERE fish_date_season = 6
GROUP BY cls
ORDER BY avg_yt_per_angler DESC

SELECT DISTINCT cls 
FROM schedule
WHERE fish_date_season = 6 AND fish_date_doy <= 15
ORDER BY cls

import pandas as pd

# Let me analyze historical S2 data to understand seasonal structure
trips_s2 = tables['trips'][tables['trips']['fish_date_season'] == 2]

# Group by day of year and class to see patterns
daily_class = trips_s2.groupby(['fish_date_doy', 'cls']).agg({
    'yt': ['sum', 'count'],
    'anglers': 'sum'
}).reset_index()
daily_class.columns = ['doy', 'cls', 'total_yt', 'num_trips', 'total_anglers']
daily_class['avg_yt_per_trip'] = daily_class['total_yt'] / daily_class['num_trips']
daily_class['avg_yt_per_angler'] = daily_class['total_yt'] / daily_class['total_anglers']

# Look at early season (April-May, doy 91-150)
early = daily_class[(daily_class['doy'] >= 91) & (daily_class['doy'] <= 150)]
print("=== S2 April-May Performance by Class ===")
print(early.groupby('cls')[['avg_yt_per_angler', 'num_trips']].agg(['mean', 'sum']).round(3))

# Look at when peaks occurred in S2
print("\n=== S2 Peak Windows (>1.0 avg yt/angler) ===")
peaks = daily_class[daily_class['avg_yt_per_angler'] > 1.0].sort_values('doy')
if len(peaks) > 0:
    print(peaks[['doy', 'cls', 'avg_yt_per_angler', 'total_yt']])
else:
    print("No peaks >1.0 yt/angler in S2")
